feature.title: A Bible-teaching ministry builds an AI answer assistant that knows when to hand you to a human
feature.why: Original reporting dated inside the window, with on-record quotes from Ligonier's CEO, about a ministry's AI tool for faith questions and the specific guardrails built into it: answers drawn only from the ministry's teaching library, a sandbox, a handoff to a real person, crisis-hotline referral for anyone who mentions suicidal thoughts, and no pretending to be human. Ligonier is not in topic memory. It moves past last week's piece on what people ask AI about faith and looks at how a ministry tries to answer safely. Barna's Oct 22 data on when Christians and pastors think AI should hand off to a human gives the context.

alsoEncouraging.title: Barna: Mom, Dad, Jesus or AI? Teens rank AI well below parents and Jesus as a source of advice
Why a Bible app team built a screen-free ring that nudges you to pray

wisdomConcern: A ministry-trained chatbot can still sound authoritative and be wrong, and a person in a spiritual crisis may confide in it instead of a pastor. Guardrails and handoffs help only if a real person is there to receive the handoff (Barna: 71% of pastors but only 32% of practicing Christians want an immediate human handoff in a spiritual crisis). Verification gaps: Ligonier Labs lists Ask Ligonier as a beta for Ministry Partners only, with no launch date, and Fox calls the app 'Grow'. The draft should say it is in limited beta and not claim a public launch.
